## Publish Listing

The single writer for a property listing’s go-live: a listing may not publish half-dressed — address, asking price, and at least one photo are enforced (photo-less listings do not get viewings). Later lifecycle moves are status edits; the publish moment never rewrites.

### Example

Natural target: the linked 14 Birchwood Lane (already live — re-running demonstrates the once-only guard).

### Non-goals

No portal syndication, no scheduled publishing.

```ts
import PublishListingCommand from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/real-estate/commands/publish-listing-command';

await new PublishListingCommand(commandContext).execute({
  listing,
  channels: ['zillow', 'realtor', 'agent-site'],
});
```

### Examples
`PropertyListing/9-harbor-view` is prepared, priced and photographed, so it publishes; `14-birchwood-lane` is already published, so the command refuses it; `1024-elm-street` is a draft with no price or photos, so the checklist blocks it.

### Channels and scheduling

Input carries `channels[]` (vocabulary in components/channel-selector; MLS always unioned in) and `scheduledDate`. Publishing is simulated (2–3s beat, mock `MLS-########`, per-channel success rows with example.com links); the result carries `channelResults[]` (`resultStatus`, not a nested `status`, because a nested field named `status` inherits the root card's status configuration), `mlsNumber`, `publishedAtIso`, `scheduled`. Draft OR prepared may publish; a future `scheduledDate` is reported back and nothing is stored or patched (a realm has no background scheduler — run it again after the time).
